value_representations.description: How one value is written as text: DICOM's value representations (PS3.5 section 6.2), each with its length limit, whether several values may be joined by the backslash, and an example. I2S defines the text of a value; the container that stores it is IFE's attribute block.

CS.description: Code String: upper-case letters, digits 0-9, the space and the underscore of the default repertoire; leading and trailing spaces are not significant. I2S writes a BOOLEAN as the CS values YES and NO, as DICOM's Burned In Annotation (0028,0301) does.

DS.description: Decimal String: a fixed-point or floating-point number of the characters 0-9, +, -, E, e and the decimal point, with no embedded space. I2S writes the shortest text that reads back to the same IEEE 754 double, and refuses a value whose text exceeds 16 bytes.

DT.description: Date Time: YYYYMMDDHHMMSS.FFFFFF&ZZXX, a Gregorian date and a 24-hour time with an optional fraction of one to six digits, then the UTC offset (& is + or -). DICOM makes the offset and the trailing components optional; I2S requires every component to the second and the offset, between -1200 and +1400, and writes the fraction to the microsecond. A second of 60 is refused, since a leap second has no point in UTC time as C++ and POSIX count it.

IS.description: Integer String: a base-10 integer of the characters 0-9 with an optional leading + or -, from -2147483648 to 2147483647.

LO.description: Long String: no control characters and no backslash, which separates values.

LT.description: Long Text: paragraphs; the control characters TAB, LF, FF and CR are allowed, and so is the backslash, since an LT holds a single value.

SH.description: Short String: no control characters and no backslash, which separates values.

ST.description: Short Text: paragraphs; the control characters TAB, LF, FF and CR are allowed, and so is the backslash, since an ST holds a single value.

UT.description: Unlimited Text: paragraphs; the control characters TAB, LF, FF and CR are allowed, and so is the backslash, since a UT holds a single value. Its limit, 2^32 - 2 bytes, fits the 32-bit value size of an IFE attribute.

value_types.description: What a key's value is, and the VRs it may be written as. Every key names exactly one value type.

TEXT.description: Text, written as the key's string VR: SH, LO, ST, LT or UT.

DATE_TIME.description: A point in time, written as a DT with its UTC offset, to the microsecond.

DECIMAL.description: A decimal number, held as an IEEE 754 double and written as a DS.

INTEGER.description: An integer from -2147483648 to 2147483647, written as an IS.

BOOLEAN.description: True or false, written as the CS values YES and NO.

identity_classes.description: Whether a key's value can identify an individual.

NONE.description: The value identifies no individual: it describes the slide or the device that scanned it.

UNDER_REVIEW.description: Whether the value can identify an individual is an open question, recorded in the key's identity note. Until it is answered, a de-identifier treats the value as identifying, unless the key's PHI flag states for the file that it is not.

keys.description: The keys a slide's I2S attributes may carry. A key's name is the attribute's key in the file.

DigitalImageIdentifier.identity_note: The DII is derived from the laboratory's accession number. Whether an accession-derived identifier identifies an individual in general is an open question for the maintainer, with research under way; for each file, its companion DigitalImageIdentifierIsPHI (DII_is_PHI) carries the answer.
DigitalImageIdentifier.description: The identifier the laboratory gave the slide when it was accessioned, carried as the digital image's identifier. I2S diverges from DICOM here: DICOM's AccessionNumber (0008,0050) identifies an imaging service request, and its Container Identifier (0040,0512) identifies the slide container; the DII is neither, so it has no DICOM keyword. Its companion DigitalImageIdentifierIsPHI (short name DII_is_PHI) tells a de-identifier whether this file's DII must be scrambled. When the DII is present and DII_is_PHI is absent, a reader and a de-identifier shall treat the DII as protected health information and scramble it.

DigitalImageIdentifierIsPHI.description: Whether this file's DigitalImageIdentifier is protected health information. true: the DII is PHI, and a de-identifier shall scramble it. false: the DII identifies no individual, and a de-identifier keeps it. Absent while the DII is present: a reader and a de-identifier shall treat the DII as PHI and scramble it, the safe default. The flag is a fact about the DII and identifies no one itself. I2S diverges from DICOM here: DICOM has no such attribute.

Manufacturer.description: Manufacturer of the scanner that produced the slide's images.

ManufacturerModelName.description: The manufacturer's model name of the scanner.

verified.title: DICOM PS3.3 2026e, C.7.5.2 Enhanced General Equipment Module

DeviceSerialNumber.identity_note: The serial number identifies one scanner. DICOM PS3.15 Annex E's Basic Application Level Confidentiality Profile removes it unless the Retain Device Identity Option is used (Table E.1-1, 2026e), and the HIPAA Safe Harbor list names "Device identifiers and serial numbers" (45 CFR 164.514(b)(2)(i)(M)); both treat a device instance as a possible link to the people it served, while neither says a scanner identifies a person. Whether it stays in I2S as identifying no individual is an open question for the maintainer (research read 2026-11-24).
DeviceSerialNumber.description: The manufacturer's serial number of the scanner.

verified.title: DICOM PS3.3 2026e, C.7.5.2 Enhanced General Equipment Module

SoftwareVersions.description: The manufacturer's designations of the scanner's software versions; one value per software component.

verified.title: DICOM PS3.3 2026e, C.7.5.1 General Equipment Module

UniqueDeviceIdentifier.identity_note: Its device identifier part names a model, shared by every unit, but its production identifier part may carry the unit's serial number (21 CFR 830.3). DICOM PS3.15 Annex E's Basic Application Level Confidentiality Profile removes it unless the Retain Device Identity Option is used (Table E.1-1, 2026e), and the HIPAA Safe Harbor list names "Device identifiers and serial numbers" (45 CFR 164.514(b)(2)(i)(M)); both treat a device instance as a possible link to the people it served, while neither says a scanner identifies a person. Whether it stays in I2S as identifying no individual is an open question for the maintainer (research read 2026-11-24).
UniqueDeviceIdentifier.description: The scanner's Unique Device Identifier, in the Human Readable Form its issuing agency defines. DICOM records it as the Unique Device Identifier of each item of the General Equipment Module's UDI Sequence, one item per issuing agency. Its VR, UT, holds a single value, so I2S carries one UDI: the one the scanner's labeler issued.

verified.title: DICOM PS3.3 2026e, C.7.10.1 General Acquisition Module

AcquisitionDateTime.identity_note: The time the slide was scanned. The HIPAA Safe Harbor list names all elements of dates, except the year, for dates directly related to an individual (45 CFR 164.514(b)(2)(i)(C)), and DICOM PS3.15's Basic Application Level Confidentiality Profile removes, empties or replaces Acquisition DateTime (action X/Z/D) unless the Retain Longitudinal Temporal Information Full Dates Option keeps it or the Modified Dates Option shifts it (PS3.15 2026e Table E.1-1, read 2026-11-24 at https://dicom.nema.org/medical/dicom/current/output/chtml/part15/chapter_E.html). A scan time is a fact of the slide, but it lies close to the dates of the patient's procedure. Whether it stays in I2S unchanged, coarsened or shifted is an open question for the maintainer.
AcquisitionDateTime.description: The date and time the acquisition of the slide's image started, with its UTC offset. A scanner writes it once, when the scan begins.
